name: confetti-burst
summary: A click-triggered confetti burst on a call-to-action card: 50 squares and circles thrown from the pointer at speed 15-25, pulled down at 9.81, spinning at 60 and fading out of existence as they fall.

quantity.description: Pieces per burst. Upstream's emitters.rate.quantity, which is what the push replaces.

colors.description: Comma-separated piece colours. Stands in for the preset's palette key. Set --fx-c1 to --fx-c5 to match so the static pieces agree.

trigger.description: Selector for the elements inside the section whose click fires a burst. Pass an empty string to make the whole section a trigger.

deviations.what: The emitters block -- name "confetti", rate quantity 50 with delay 0, life count 0 / duration 0.1 / delay 0.4 -- is dropped, and the burst comes from container.particles.push(quantity, position) on a click instead.
deviations.why: The emitters plugin is not registered in the vendored @tsparticles/slim 4.3.2 bundle, so the preset as written loads and paints nothing. Pushing a batch in on an event is the same shape of burst -- the count comes straight from rate.quantity -- and the per-piece lifetime the emitter's life gave comes from the opacity animation the preset already carries: it starts at max, runs to min at speed 3, and destroy: "min" removes the piece there. What is genuinely not reachable is continuous or timed emission, which is a vendor change rather than an effect change.

deviations.what: particles.tilt, particles.roll and particles.wobble are all dropped.
deviations.why: None of the three updaters is in the vendored slim bundle. They are what gives real confetti its paper flutter and the light and dark faces of a spinning piece, so this is a good burst rather than a photoreal confetti cannon -- say so before shipping it as one. What survives is rotate, which is registered, so the pieces spin in plane but do not flip.

deviations.what: motion: { disable: true } is dropped, and under prefers-reduced-motion no container is created at all.
deviations.why: That flag forces the animation to run whatever the reader has asked for, which is the exact inverse of this library's contract. Nothing is lost by honouring the preference here: the section is a card with a working button, and the burst is decoration on top of it.

deviations.what: fullScreen goes from { enable: true, zIndex: 100 } to { enable: false }, and the background block is dropped.
deviations.why: fullScreen puts the canvas in a fixed layer over the whole page, which is right for a demo and wrong for a section that has to sit in a page beside other sections -- two of these on one page would stack two full-page canvases. The background is the same seam starfield's meta.json records: the section's CSS owns it.

deviations.what: palette: "confetti" is dropped and the piece colours become an explicit paint.fill.color list.
deviations.why: A palette name is resolved by the presets package's own theme registry, which a vendored engine bundle does not carry, so loading the key would leave the colour unset. The five defaults are a confetti set and they are an option, so a section can match its own brand.

deviations.what: The canvas is layered under the copy card, and the trigger button sits outside the card in open section rather than inside it.
deviations.why: Upstream's fullScreen canvas paints over everything, and measured mid-burst that takes the body copy under it from 10:1 to 1.01:1 -- this library holds text to 4.5:1 against the busiest live frame, so pieces cannot cross it. Putting the canvas under the card fixes the ratio but hides the burst behind it when the trigger is inside; moving the trigger out is what gives the throw open section to spread into. Both halves are one decision, which is why the section is built the way it is.

deviations.what: A keyboard activation of the trigger (a click event with detail 0) bursts from the control's own centre rather than from the pointer coordinates.
deviations.why: A button reached by Tab and pressed with Enter fires a click whose clientX and clientY are 0, which would throw every burst from the section's top left corner. Upstream never meets this case because an emitter has a fixed position and no trigger at all.

deviations.what: Upstream is a preset registered on the engine and applied by name; here the options object is passed straight to engine.load().
deviations.why: A preset only exists to be looked up by name, which a single-effect module has no use for. The options object it registers is what actually configures the container, and that is what travels.
